method: Read public primary British Library catalogue JSON and EAP metadata, inspect documented IIIF v3 manifests, download published image/jpeg bodies, and visually inspect local files. No application, server, browser or tests were run; no anti-bot bypass was used. This file is evidence and research candidates only.
decision: No photo is preferred or eligible for active integration. Public access and a valid licence do not establish the exact photographed subject.

hierarchyInspection.finding: All node titles inspected for target aliases. Named Berkut and mixed Bazar series exist; Gyaur entries collide with other sites; no Eres, Davletgirey or Puljay match.
hierarchyInspection.caveat: A missing catalogue title does not prove that a destination has no photographs elsewhere or within unidentified aerial survey material.

licenseEvidence.evidence: Each checked item contains the Creative Commons BY-NC 4.0 link; manifest rights fields repeat it. Manifest image bodies supply exact public JPEG URLs.
licenseEvidence.author: Khorezmian Archaeological-Ethnographic Expedition of the Academy of Sciences of the USSR
licenseEvidence.originalCustodian: Institute of Ethnology and Anthropology, Russian Academy of Sciences, Moscow, Russian Federation
licenseEvidence.restrictions: Noncommercial use, attribution, archive shelfmark and original custodian must be preserved. Academic tourism context and licence permission still require exact subject verification.

records.finding: The archive has several Gyaur-Kala entries, but none establishes the exact Sultan Uvays destination. Do not substitute Mizdakhkan or Turkmenistan sites.

sourcesChecked.finding: Gyaur-Kala 1 and surroundings; place of origin Turkmenistan, so unsuitable for Sultan Uvays.
Gyaur-Kala 2; place only Central Asia. The aerial frame shows a roughly square enclosure with handwritten measurements; no evidence establishes Sultan Uvays.

researchOnlyDownloads.originalCustodian: Institute of Ethnology and Anthropology, Russian Academy of Sciences, Moscow, Russian Federation
researchOnlyDownloads.modifications: None; source JPEG response preserved unchanged.

records.finding: EAP1075/1/90 names Bazar-Kala together with Dzhanbas-Kala and Kum-Baskan-Kala. Forty-seven of 115 canvases were downloaded and visually inspected, including the first 20 and later fortress-containing frames. Individual item titles repeat the mixed-series title, so a photographed fortress cannot honestly be marked as Bazar-Kala solely from membership in this series.

sourcesChecked.extent: 105 aerial photographs and 10 notes; 115 TIFF scans
sourcesChecked.finding: Mixed series includes the correct destination, but frame-level site identity is unresolved.
Primary regional tourism subject reference, but not covered by the national Uzbekistan Travel reuse grant. Watermark credits a third-party research institute.
Original custodian's copy of Tolstov's book identifies an aerial Bazar-Kala figure. Web text located the figure but PDF image retrieval did not complete, so no pixel/shape match is claimed.
